recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Further work on related vital signs applicability or invariant semantics should remain with the separate Jira issues that own those topics, not with FHIR-26964.
issue_request: FHIR-26964 is an Applied/Persuasive OO clarification for the FHIR-core Observation vital signs profile. It asked to clarify the vs-1/vsp-1 human-readable description for Observation.effective[x] so dateTime values are understood to be precise at least to the day, rather than only exactly to the day.
initial_application: The Jira comment records that Robert Hausam updated the effective[x] human-readable text and applied git 3602472e30. That commit changed source/observation/structuredefinition-profile-vitalsigns.xml from "precise to the day" to "precise at least to the day" for the vsp-1 constraint human value.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Observation as an active resource, and source/observation/structuredefinition-profile-vitalsigns.xml is the current vital signs StructureDefinition source in that active resource folder. The originating Zulip thread confirms the intended interpretation was minimum day precision. Later nearby vital-signs issues, including FHIR-29654 about invariant behavior with effective[x] types and FHIR-41426 about broader vital signs applicability, do not change the FHIR-26964 wording decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already contains the requested "precise at least to the day" human-readable constraint text, matching the applied Jira comment and the implementing commit.
